objectives.title: Represent a Goose in Court
objectives.task: defend a goose accused of stealing the mayor’s campaign hats

climax.text: The judge asks whether the hats were stolen or given away. The goose has arrived wearing all seventeen. The mayor insists this proves something.

choices.label: Prove the hats were campaign gifts
choices.win: You show the gift labels. The judge dismisses the theft charge.
choices.lose: The mayor disputes a missing label. The goose objects by biting you.

onWin.memory: You show the gift labels. The judge dismisses the theft charge.

choices.label: Ask the crowd to confirm the giveaway
choices.win: The crowd remembers the giveaway. The mayor withdraws the charge rather than lose their votes.
choices.lose: The mayor calls his own supporters. The crowd jostles you away from the stand.

onWin.memory: The crowd remembers the giveaway. The mayor withdraws the charge rather than lose their votes.

choices.label: Keep the goose still for the verdict
choices.win: The goose stays quiet long enough for the judge to acquit it. Then it steals the gavel.
choices.lose: The goose grabs the verdict before it is read. You are knocked over trying to retrieve it.

onWin.memory: The goose stays quiet long enough for the judge to acquit it. Then it steals the gavel.

objectives.title: Exorcise the Self-Checkout
objectives.task: settle a ghost’s unfinished purchase at a grocery checkout

climax.text: The ghost has its receipt, but the checkout still announces an unexpected customer in the bagging area. You need to clear the final transaction so it can leave.

choices.label: Convince the register the sale is complete
choices.win: The register closes the transaction. The ghost takes its milk and finally moves on.
choices.lose: The register demands another supervisor. Its alarm sends you staggering into the carts.

onWin.memory: The register closes the transaction. The ghost takes its milk and finally moves on.

choices.label: Reset the checkout safely
choices.win: You finish the transaction and restart the register. The ghost departs through a pleasantly quiet wall.
choices.lose: The register rejects the reset and shocks your fingers.

onWin.memory: You finish the transaction and restart the register. The ghost departs through a pleasantly quiet wall.

choices.label: Pull the stuck receipt free
choices.win: The last piece of receipt comes loose. The ghost leaves with its proof of purchase.
choices.lose: The receipt tangles around your boot. The ghost pulls harder and topples you into the baskets.

onWin.memory: The last piece of receipt comes loose. The ghost leaves with its proof of purchase.

text.f: A goose has been arrested for stealing the mayor's hat. It refuses to speak to anyone who cannot honk. The officer hands you seventeen previous complaints.
text.c: The goose is accused of stealing the mayor's hat. It demands a lawyer who can honk. The officer says this is the most reasonable thing it has asked for.
text.x: The goose stole the mayor's hat and now wants a lawyer. It refuses to speak until you honk. The officer calls it a difficult little bastard.

choices.label: Honk until the goose cooperates
choices.win: The goose tells you the hats were abandoned campaign gifts. You ask to examine them.
choices.lose: Your honk sounds like an insult. The goose bites your hand.

onWin.memory: The goose tells you the hats were abandoned campaign gifts. You ask to examine them.

choices.label: Hire an interpreter
choices.win: The interpreter explains that the goose claims the mayor gave the hats away.
choices.lose: The interpreter refuses to work with this goose again.

onWin.memory: The interpreter explains that the goose claims the mayor gave the hats away.

choices.label: Read the officer’s complaints
choices.win: You find a note saying the mayor distributed hats during his campaign.
choices.lose: You turn the pages too slowly. The goose adds your finger to its list of objections.

onWin.memory: You find a note saying the mayor distributed hats during his campaign.

text.f: The evidence locker holds seventeen identical mayoral hats. Each says FREE CAMPAIGN GIFT inside. The officer insists the goose could not possibly need seventeen.
text.c: Every hat says FREE CAMPAIGN GIFT. The officer's case now rests on the claim that seventeen free hats is simply too many hats.
text.x: All seventeen hats say FREE CAMPAIGN GIFT. The officer still wants a conviction. Apparently the goose is guilty of being an irritating little bastard.

choices.label: Show the judge the labels
choices.win: The judge agrees the hats were gifts. The case can proceed with the evidence corrected.
choices.lose: You grab the wrong hat. The goose bites you before you can show the label.

onWin.memory: The judge agrees the hats were gifts. The case can proceed with the evidence corrected.

choices.label: Measure the hats against the goose
choices.win: You prove the hats were made for campaign supporters of every size.
choices.lose: The goose refuses the fitting and chases you around the evidence table.

onWin.memory: You prove the hats were made for campaign supporters of every size.

text.f: A ghost is haunting a grocery checkout. It paid for milk just before it died, but the register says payment failed. It will not leave without a receipt.
text.c: The ghost paid for its milk and then died in line. The register says payment failed. Customer service says it needs a living signature.
text.x: The ghost is owed a receipt for milk. Customer service wants a living signature. It has been arguing with these bastards since it died.

choices.label: Match the payment to the register
choices.win: You find the payment in the register’s records. A supervisor must authorize the refund.
choices.lose: The register prints twenty feet of errors. You slip on the paper.

onWin.memory: You find the payment in the register’s records. A supervisor must authorize the refund.

choices.label: Pay the disputed milk charge
choices.win: The register accepts the payment. A supervisor must now approve the ghost’s receipt.
choices.lose: The register refuses the payment.

onWin.memory: The register accepts the payment. A supervisor must now approve the ghost’s receipt.

choices.label: Lift the register to check its records
choices.win: You find the trapped receipt beneath the register. It still needs a supervisor’s stamp.
choices.lose: The register’s cord pulls tight. You drop it on your foot.

onLose.memory: The register’s cord pulls tight. You drop it on your foot.

text.f: The supervisor agrees the ghost paid. She says refunds require a customer survey. The ghost asks whether being dead counts as a poor shopping experience.
text.c: The supervisor insists on a customer survey before approving the refund. The ghost asks whether 'never shop here again' is meant to include the afterlife.
text.x: The supervisor agrees the ghost paid, then demands a customer survey. The ghost says dying in line was already a pretty fucking clear review.

choices.label: Ask the supervisor to approve an exception
choices.win: She approves the receipt. The ghost finally has proof of purchase.
choices.lose: She directs you to the complaints desk. A falling stack of baskets blocks your way.

onWin.memory: She approves the receipt. The ghost finally has proof of purchase.

choices.label: Complete the customer survey
choices.win: You finish the survey. The ghost collects its receipt and stops haunting the register.
choices.lose: The survey restarts on the last question. The ghost loses patience and shoves the register into you.

onWin.memory: You finish the survey. The ghost collects its receipt and stops haunting the register.

text.f: The dragon has moved its gold onto a raft beyond the tax inspector's reach. It calls this an offshore account. The raft is leaking.
text.c: The dragon's offshore account is a raft three feet from shore. It is leaking gold through the floor. The inspector is enjoying the audit immensely.
text.x: The dragon has put its gold on a leaking raft and called it an offshore account. The inspector says it is the stupidest tax dodge he has ever bloody seen.

choices.label: Explain that the raft is still taxable
choices.win: The inspector accepts the declaration and helps secure the raft.
choices.lose: The dragon refuses the explanation and shoves you into the shallows.

onWin.memory: The inspector accepts the declaration and helps secure the raft.

choices.label: Bring the gold back without tipping the raft
choices.win: You recover the gold before the raft sinks. The inspector starts counting.
choices.lose: The raft tips. You fall between the gold crates and the dock.

onLose.memory: The raft tips. You fall between the gold crates and the dock.

choices.label: Buy waterproof boxes for the records
choices.win: You keep the tax records dry while the inspector secures the raft.
choices.lose: The supply shop has no waterproof boxes.

onWin.memory: You keep the tax records dry while the inspector secures the raft.

text.f: Gregory the soup has organized a walkout. The other dishes agree they should not be eaten, but none can reach the kitchen door. The chef is fetching bowls.
text.c: Gregory has persuaded the other dishes to walk out. The plan has reached a small difficulty: most of his supporters do not have legs.
text.x: Gregory has organized a kitchen walkout. None of his supporters can walk. The chef is fetching bowls, so you had better sort the bloody transport.

choices.label: Arrange a tray for the escaping dishes
choices.win: You load the dishes onto a serving cart and wheel them away from the chef.
choices.lose: The overloaded cart tips into your legs. The kitchen staff hears the crash.

onWin.memory: You load the dishes onto a serving cart and wheel them away from the chef.

choices.label: Print signs declaring the food alive
choices.win: The staff stops serving the dishes while a manager checks the complaint.
choices.lose: The printer is unavailable.

onWin.memory: The staff stops serving the dishes while a manager checks the complaint.

choices.label: Hold the door against the kitchen staff
choices.win: You hold the door while Gregory’s supporters reach the exit.
choices.lose: A waiter pushes a bread cart through the door and knocks you down.

onLose.memory: A waiter pushes a bread cart through the door and knocks you down.

text.f: The manager will release Gregory if the staff agrees. Gregory argues that talking food deserves a choice. The chef argues that soup is much harder to sell once it talks.
text.c: The manager has called a staff vote. Gregory asks for the right to leave. The chef says he has already sold six portions and would prefer nobody mention that.
text.x: The staff is voting on Gregory's freedom. The chef is worried about refunds. Gregory points out that being eaten is rather more of a bloody inconvenience.

choices.label: Ask the staff whether they would eat Gregory
choices.win: Nobody volunteers. The manager agrees that Gregory may leave.
choices.lose: The chef describes his recipe. The hungry staff crowds you away from the table.

onWin.memory: Nobody volunteers. The manager agrees that Gregory may leave.

choices.label: Remind them that Gregory asked for help
choices.win: The staff backs Gregory’s request. The manager reluctantly agrees to release him.
choices.lose: The chef calls it part of the dinner show. A waiter bundles you out of the meeting.

onWin.memory: The staff backs Gregory’s request. The manager reluctantly agrees to release him.

text.f: The tower's support line has played the same lute note for two hours. A clerk finally answers and asks you to identify the note as a security check.
text.c: Two hours on hold, one lute note. The support clerk now wants its name before discussing the password. The musician looks as tired as you feel.
text.x: Two hours of the same bloody lute note. Support finally answers, then asks you to identify it. The wizard is ready to attack the instrument.

choices.label: Identify the note for the support clerk
choices.win: You identify the note. The clerk starts the password reset.
choices.lose: You give the wrong note. The security alarm knocks you off the doorstep.

onWin.memory: You identify the note. The clerk starts the password reset.

choices.label: Wait for a senior support clerk
choices.win: A senior clerk answers and authorizes a reset. You exchange exhausted sympathies.
choices.lose: The line sends you back to the beginning. You slump backward off the waiting bench.

onWin.memory: A senior clerk answers and authorizes a reset. You exchange exhausted sympathies.

choices.label: Ask the lute player for a hint
choices.win: The musician quietly names the note. Support accepts your answer.
choices.lose: The musician calls security instead. A guard escorts you out with unnecessary force.

onWin.memory: The musician quietly names the note. Support accepts your answer.
